title: NIST FSE 2008: fires in an ISO 9705 room, the tests with a door of 0.4 m or more, first window (NIST, Lock et al.)
reference: Lock, A., Bundy, M., Johnsson, E. L., Hamins, A., Ko, G. H., Hwang, C. and Fuss, P. (2008), as described in the FDS Validation Guide (NIST SP 1018-3), section NIST Full-Scale Enclosure Experiments, 2008
notice: Measurements from NIST's Fire Research Division Experimental Database (github.com/firemodels/exp) and test conditions from NIST's FDS validation inputs (github.com/firemodels/fds), both carrying NIST's notice: NIST-developed works, not subject to copyright protection within the United States; acknowledge the National Institute of Standards and Technology as the source; modified works should note the date and nature of any change. Changed here (2026-11-11): reduced to the numbers compared by tools/calibration/validation-suite.mjs (thermocouple trees reduced by Janssens and Tran's method at each measured time; point readings within the compared windows; geometry and burner read from the FDS inputs).
heldOut: never used to fit any solver parameter (fire-calibration-plan-2026-11-11.md, section 12)

tests.ventilation: door 0.8 m wide, 1.9 to 2.0 m high

burner.ramp: FDS MASS_FLUX 0.04780 kg/(m2 s) x 1.00 m2 x 'fire_ramp' x 50 MJ/kg, to the guide's first window's end (580 s)
burner.radiantSource: FDS's default for METHANE (the input sets 0 because FDS there computes the flame's radiation; this solver's burner needs a fraction)

fuel.name: methane
fuel.source: natural gas (93 % methane) as methane; no soot; CO2 by the carbon balance

tests.ventilation: door 0.4 m wide, 1.9 to 2.0 m high

burner.radiantSource: FDS's default for N-HEPTANE (the input sets 0 because FDS there computes the flame's radiation; this solver's burner needs a fraction)

fuel.name: heptane
fuel.source: heptane; soot 0.0149 and CO 0.008 from the FDS input's REAC; CO2 by the carbon balance
